Proposed sale of Eagle 31 to Ecuador

In the 1920s, the Ecuadorean Navy consisted of the 750-ton ex-Chilean torpedo gunboat Libertador Bolivar (ex-Almirante Simpson), launched in 1896, and the gunboat Cotapaxi launched in 1884. In 1926 it was determined that Libertador Bolivar was no longer considered repairable, and from 1928 strenuous efforts were made to obtain funds to purchase a replacement vessel. In the first months of 1930, naval leaders struggling to persuade the Government to acquire at least one vessel submitted a proposal to purchase two small destroyers, with a budget of 100,000 sucres (approx. US$20,000) each, saved over the preceding two years. However, in the following year’s budget that sum had disappeared - absorbed back into state expenditure. Approaches were made to the USN to acquire an Eagle boat, and to the Chilean Government to obtain old Almirante Lynch class destroyers.

Eagle Boats were a class of sixty 500-ton, 200-foot patrol vessels built by the US during World War I. Eagle 31 had been sold to private interests on 18 May 1923. In July 1930 an American firm proposed to sell the ex-Eagle 31 (PE-31) to Ecuador without armament, but in such a condition that she could be subsequently armed by the purchaser. Britain submitted a mild protest regarding this proposal. The US answered that for the time being the matter was not being proceeded with, but if the Ecuadorean Government later decided to go through with the proposal, the US would consult the other signatory powers. In November 1930, there is reference to a proposal to sell two Eagle boats to Ecuador, however nothing further had been heard since the Ecuadorian Government had been informed regarding the conditions under which the vessels would be sold.

Six Almirante Lynch class destroyers were ordered by Chile from Britain before World War I, but only two (Almirante Lynch and Almirante Condell) had been delivered prior to the outbreak, when the remaining four were taken over for the Royal Navy. The three RN vessels which survived the war (Tipperary ex-Almirante Riveros was sunk at the Battle of Jutland) were repurchased by Chile in 1920 (Almirante Williams ex-Botha, Almirante Uribe ex-Broke, and Almirante Riveros ex-Faulknor). The three returned ships had been significantly altered and are normally considered a separate class (the Almirante Williams class). No further information has been located regarding the reported request by Ecuador to procure members of this class.
